title: Best Social Media Privacy Tools Compared
metaDescription: DuckDuckGo's browser, Ghostery, Privacy Badger and Incognito Browser (which we make) compared on limiting tracking by Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and more.
intro: Social media platforms collect vast amounts of personal data, often without users fully understanding the extent. From targeted advertising to data sharing with third parties, your privacy is constantly at risk. This page compares four browser tools that limit how social platforms track you.

products.name: Incognito Browser
products.tagline: Android browser that stays in private mode and wipes cookies and sessions when you exit
pros: Social sites' cookies and sessions are wiped when you exit, so logins don't carry over
A setting switches cookies off entirely
Built-in ad blocker with a High Security Blocking option
cons: Tracker blocking, privacy alerts and social-platform guides are not among its listed features
Protects browsing only, not social media apps
Android only: no iOS, desktop or web version
Google Play's Data safety section says it may collect crash logs and diagnostics

products.name: Privacy Badger
products.tagline: EFF's tracker blocker that stops third parties seen tracking people across sites
pros: Blocks trackers automatically, with no filter lists to manage
Replaces embedded social buttons and posts with click-to-load placeholders

products.name: DuckDuckGo Browser
products.tagline: Privacy browser for phones and computers, with tracker blocking on by default
pros: Blocks social media trackers by default
Privacy Dashboard shows what was blocked on each site
Privacy policy says it doesn't collect personal information

products.name: Ghostery
products.tagline: Tracker and ad blocker that shows which trackers each site loads
pros: Extensions for desktop browsers, a Safari extension on iPhone and iPad, and a Firefox add-on on Android
cons: Its Private Browser app was discontinued (announced December 2024)
Protects browsing only, not social media apps

features.name: Social Media Tracker Blocking
features.description: Prevents Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and other platforms from tracking you across the web

incognito-browser.note: Tracker blocking is not among its listed features; cookies and sessions are wiped when you exit

privacy-badger.note: Blocks trackers that ignore its opt-out signals, using a tracker list EFF keeps updated

features.name: Platform-Specific Privacy Settings
features.description: Tools and guides for optimizing privacy settings on each social media platform

duckduckgo-browser.note: No in-app guidance for social platforms' settings

ghostery.note: No in-app guidance for social platforms' settings

features.name: Data Download Assistance
features.description: Help with downloading and understanding your data from social media platforms

ghostery.note: Shows the trackers on a page, but doesn't help you download your platform data

features.name: Cross-Platform Protection
features.description: Prevents data sharing between different social media platforms and third parties

incognito-browser.note: Switching cookies off stops cookie-based tracking across sites; cookies are also wiped when you exit

features.name: Mobile App Protection
features.description: Privacy protection for social media apps on smartphones and tablets

incognito-browser.note: Protects browsing only, not social media apps

duckduckgo-browser.note: App Tracking Protection (Android only) blocks third-party trackers inside other apps

ghostery.note: Its Private Browser app was discontinued; the extensions protect browsing, not apps

features.name: Real-Time Privacy Alerts
features.description: Notifications about privacy threats and data collection attempts

duckduckgo-browser.note: Privacy Dashboard shows the trackers blocked on each site

verdict.summary: On these six criteria DuckDuckGo's browser scores highest: it blocks third-party trackers by default and, on Android, its App Tracking Protection also blocks trackers inside other apps. Ghostery comes next, with the most detailed tracker alerts. Privacy Badger comes third: it is free, open source and needs no setup, but it runs only as a browser extension and has no iOS version. Incognito Browser, which we make, scores lowest: it can switch cookies off and wipes them when you exit, but it doesn't list tracker blocking or privacy alerts. None of the four offers guides to each platform's privacy settings or helps you download your data, so do those in each platform's own settings.

bestFor.reason: Highest score here; blocks trackers by default and, on Android, blocks third-party trackers inside other apps
Detailed tracker identification and customizable blocking options
Set-and-forget tracker blocking from the non-profit EFF

pro_tips: Layer your tools: a browser that blocks trackers plus a tracker-blocking extension catches more than either alone, if your browser accepts extensions.
Regularly review and tighten your privacy settings on each platform, as they frequently change their policies and defaults.
Download your data from social platforms annually to see what information they're collecting about you.
Consider using separate browsers for social media and other activities to limit cross-site tracking.
Enable two-factor authentication on all social accounts to prevent unauthorized access and potential data breaches.

faqs.question: Do I need to pay for social media privacy protection?
faqs.answer: No. Privacy Badger and DuckDuckGo's browser are free, and Ghostery's tracker blocking is free; its Contributor plans are optional extras. Incognito Browser, which we make, is free, with an optional Incognito Pro subscription.

faqs.question: Will privacy tools break social media functionality?
faqs.answer: Some features may be affected, particularly targeted ads and cross-platform sharing. However, core functionality like posting, messaging, and viewing content typically works normally. Most tools allow you to whitelist specific features if needed.

faqs.question: How often should I update my social media privacy settings?
faqs.answer: Review your settings every 3-6 months, as platforms frequently introduce new features and change default settings. Also check immediately after major platform updates or when you receive privacy policy notifications.

faqs.question: Can I protect my privacy on social media apps or only on browsers?
faqs.answer: Browser tools protect what you do in a browser, not inside the social media apps. On Android, DuckDuckGo's App Tracking Protection blocks many third-party trackers inside other apps. Otherwise, review each app's privacy settings and permissions, or use the platform's website in a browser instead of the app.

faqs.question: What's the biggest privacy risk on social media?
faqs.answer: Cross-platform data sharing is the biggest concern - platforms track your activity across the web to build detailed profiles. This data is used for targeted advertising and may be shared with third parties, making comprehensive tracker blocking essential.
